 Order

The petitioners, vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, seek quashing of FIR No. 662/2016 dated 14.08.2016 registered under Sections 498A/354/406/34 IPC at PS:
Neb Sarai, Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom in view of the Settlement dated 07.05.2021 arrived at between the parties before the Counseling Cell, Family Courts, Saket, New Delhi.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Settlement dated 07.05.2021 [Annexure-C] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
CRL.M.C. 1924/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/12/2023 at 01:10:59 3.
Petitioner nos.1 to 8 as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.

sentences.text: Learned APP accepts notice.
He confirms that since the FIR involves matrimonial disputes, he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.
6. Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 18.04.2022.

She further affirms the Settlement dated 07.05.2021 whereby the petitioner no.1 has already paid her a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- and the remaining amount of Rs.1,25,000/- has been handed over to the respondent no.2 vide DD no.411597 issued on 15.12.2023 [Punjab National Bank] in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr. (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.
CRL.M.C. 1924/2023 page 2 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.

Accordingly, the petition is allowed and FIR No.662/2016 dated 14.08.2016 registered under Sections 498A/354/406/34 IPC registered at PS: Neb Sarai, District South Delhi and all proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.

9. Needless to state that in view of the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ganesh v. Sudhir Kumar Srivastava (2020) 20 SCC 787, the settlement arrived at between the parties resulting in closure of all criminal proceedings inter se the parties by way of the present order will, in no way,
effect the rights of the children of the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2 namely Master Varun Gupta vis-a-vis his parents, as may be available under law, in any manner whatsoever.
